section_summary: The section opens with Senator Harry F. Byrd’s inquiry to the State Department about an insurance society’s allegation that a U.S. mission intended to impose compulsory health insurance on Japan. It then contains a transmittal and two copies of a Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers public health and welfare bulletin for November 30–December 6, 1947, with weekly and monthly disease reports. The bulletin covers hospital electricity and bed capacity, medical supplies, welfare institutions, professional training, disease control, narcotics, and health insurance facilities.

subfiles.title: Senator Byrd’s inquiry to Secretary Marshall
subfiles.about: Byrd forwards E. H. Mears’s communication and requests the State Department’s comment.
subfiles.summary: Forwards Mears’s inquiry and asks for comment.

subfiles.title: E. H. Mears’s letter to Senator Byrd
subfiles.about: Mears asks whether a confidential insurance society report accurately describes plans to socialize medicine in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses an insurance society memorandum and asks Byrd to verify its claims about compulsory medicine in Japan.

subfiles.title: Social Security Mission to Japan
subfiles.from: Insurance Economics Society of America; flash report from Marjorie Shearon
subfiles.about: The report alleges that U.S. officials planned to introduce compulsory health insurance in Japan and urges political protest.
subfiles.summary: Alleges that a forthcoming U.S. mission will press Japan to adopt compulsory health insurance, names purported participants, and urges members to contact Congress.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of Senator Byrd’s inquiry
subfiles.from: Carl Marcy, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: The State Department acknowledges Byrd’s letter and promises a later response after officials review the allegations.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges receipt and promises to relay officials’ views later.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Public Health and Welfare Section Weekly Bulletin No. 49
subfiles.about: The Acting Political Adviser sends five copies of the occupation headquarters’ weekly health and welfare bulletin.
subfiles.summary: Transmits five copies of Bulletin No. 49 and says future bulletins will be forwarded without covering despatches.

subfiles.title: Handwritten assessment of the attached health reports
subfiles.about: A reader comments on the technical detail and possible usefulness of the attached reports.
subfiles.summary: Calls the reports detailed and technical and questions their usefulness to Far Eastern Affairs.

subfiles.title: Public Health and Welfare Section Weekly Bulletin No. 49
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; Crawford F. Sams
subfiles.to: Military government and Japanese public health officials
subfiles.about: The bulletin reports on welfare, nursing, medical supplies, disease prevention, hospital capacity, and health insurance for November 30–December 6, 1947.
subfiles.summary: The bulletin describes relief shipments, food rations for children’s institutions, nursing education, hospital electricity shortages, DDT and drug distribution, and narcotics enforcement. It urges training for prefectural health staff and sets out tuberculosis and typhus control measures. It reports 3,391 civilian hospitals with 212,012 beds, 98,872 occupied beds, and 299,512 outpatients, along with grants for health insurance treatment facilities.

subfiles.title: Weekly report of communicable diseases in Japan, week ending November 29, 1947
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A digest and prefectural tables record weekly disease cases, deaths, rates, and comparisons with 1946.
subfiles.summary: The report records 10,095 communicable disease cases for the week, led by tuberculosis, pneumonia, measles, whooping cough, and influenza. It discusses trends in diphtheria, dysentery, typhoid, malaria, typhus, and other infections. Prefectural tables give current and cumulative counts, followed by comparisons with 1946 and a venereal disease summary.

subfiles.title: Monthly report of communicable diseases in Japan, five weeks ending November 29, 1947
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: A monthly digest and prefectural tables compare November 1947 disease incidence and deaths with October 1947 and November 1946.
subfiles.summary: The report counts 6,400 cases and 881 deaths for twelve reported diseases during the five-week period. Diphtheria and scarlet fever rose, while most other reported disease rates fell or remained steady. Tables provide prefectural cases, deaths, and rates, with corrections to the October report.

subfiles.title: Second copy of Public Health and Welfare Section Weekly Bulletin No. 49
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers; Crawford F. Sams
subfiles.to: Military government and Japanese public health officials
subfiles.about: A second copy repeats the bulletin for November 30–December 6, 1947.
subfiles.summary: This copy repeats the welfare, nursing, supply, preventive medicine, hospital capacity, and health insurance reports on pages 7–17. Its medical service section again reports 3,391 civilian hospitals and 212,012 beds, of which 98,872 were occupied.

subfiles.title: Second copy of weekly communicable disease report, week ending November 29, 1947
subfiles.from: Public Health and Welfare Section, General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
subfiles.about: The attached second copy repeats the weekly disease digest and prefectural tables and continues beyond this section.
subfiles.summary: The digest and tables repeat the weekly counts for major communicable diseases, including 5,440 tuberculosis cases and 2,092 pneumonia cases. Pages 46–53 cover the digest and tables through pneumonia and influenza; the attachment continues after page 53.
